lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The profile link looks abbreviated rather than like a standard profile URL.
items.because: It should be a complete, working, clickable URL.

items.says: The résumé includes a date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They are not needed for most U.S. applications and can invite irrelevant bias.

items.says: Clarify whether the MBA was completed or expected.
items.because: The dates alone can leave its status unclear.

items.says: Consider placing Experience before Education.
items.because: You have several years of work experience, unless this is a student-recruiting résumé centered on the MBA.

items.says: Clarify whether the 35% conversion increase is relative or in percentage points.
Give the measurement period or comparison basis for the conversion increase.
Make the attribution of the conversion increase to the new flow defensible.
items.because: “After” does not establish that the new flow caused the change.

items.says: Clarify the scope of “all merchants.”
Explain what “two weeks ahead of plan” means.
Include a user or business outcome if one was measured.
State the currency of the annual loss figure.
Explain how the annual loss figure was estimated or annualized.
Make your role in setting the roadmap priority clear and supportable.
items.because: The claim that this work set the priority is strong.

items.says: Standardize the British spelling “analysed” to match U.S. English.
items.because: The U.S. locations and other wording suggest U.S. English.

items.says: Give the starting queue size or the period used to calculate the reduction by half.
Add the effect of ticket closure on merchants or onboarding, if available.
items.because: Ticket volume may not be the strongest product-management evidence.

items.says: Add the finding from the onboarding comparison.
items.because: The bullet describes an approach without a result.

items.says: Explain how you accounted for merchants choosing whether to opt in.
Combine or remove overlapping onboarding evidence.
items.because: This bullet may be redundant with the following onboarding result.

items.says: Specify the measurement period for the time-to-first-payment reduction.
Clarify the pilot’s scope.
Confirm that the 2,300 merchants are the population measured.
Make sure the reduction can fairly be attributed to the redesign.
The bullet presents excluding weather delays as a reduction in actual late deliveries.
items.because: Changing the reporting definition is not an operational improvement and risks appearing to manipulate the metric.

items.says: Add the baseline or time period for the 30% pick-error reduction.
The verb “prepares” is in present tense despite the role ending in 2023.
Clarify your contribution to the forecast pack or the process’s effect.
items.because: The bullet emphasizes recurring duties rather than outcomes.

items.says: Clarify whether the 1,800 driver hours are measured savings or an estimate.
State the period used to calculate the annual savings figure.
Make sure the project’s ongoing status is accurate.
Clarify whether 3,100 students were reached, registered, or active.
State how the food quantity was measured.
Clarify what “its first year” refers to.
Clarify the comparison period for weekly active users.
Avoid attributing all user growth to the reminders without support.
Clarify the time period behind the reduction in staff cover shifts.
Make the relationship between volunteer coverage and fewer staff cover shifts clear.
State what you produced, recommended, or helped clinic managers decide.
items.because: The bullet describes an activity rather than your contribution or impact.

items.says: Clarify your role in mapping intake and shortening the form.
items.because: The passive construction obscures what you did.

items.says: Quantify what changed about the form or intake process, if possible.
Explain what staff adoption achieved.
The merchant first-payment result is misplaced under the hospital practicum and duplicates a Harbor Payments result.
items.because: It is unrelated to the named client and could make a reader question the résumé’s accuracy.

items.says: The “A/B testing” skill is not clearly supported.
items.because: The Harbor Payments opt-in comparison is not necessarily an A/B test.

items.says: Use a consistent style for numbers and units.
items.because: Currency, percentages, time periods, and food quantities should be presented consistently.

items.says: Keep bullet indentation and line wrapping consistent.
items.because: Wrapping should not make a bullet look like a continuation of another item.
